experiment.name: interrupt-smoothness
experiment.question: Can additive general-purpose prompt clauses close the stable qa-bench interrupt failures without regressing passing cases, and do they generalize to a held-out set?
experiment.metric: qa-bench hard-PASS rate (grade.ts: deterministic gates + gemini-3.5-flash judge)
experiment.threshold_rule: Strictly dominate baseline on dev (fix targets, regress 0) AND regress 0 behaviour classes on the sealed held-out test set.

verdict.rationale: iter3 strictly dominates on dev (mean 9.7/11 vs baseline 7.7/11 — ~4x the +-0.5-case within-arm variance, clearing the +9pp threshold) and on the sealed held-out test regresses 0 (T1/T2/T6 stay PASS) while gaining T3 (engage-already-revealed), proving that fix generalizes. The held-out N=6 gives wide CIs (crossing zero) so it is a directional generalization sanity-check, not a powered significance test. Ship iter3. Residuals documented (not chased): T4/C6 planner-side math leak, T5/C5 confusion-restart (untargeted), C7 climax leak (no-early-reveal clause was neutral).
